item.title: TODAY IN HISTORY: Space Shuttle Columbia Breaks Apart, Seven Astronauts Killed (2003)
item.description: TODAY IN HISTORY: On February 1, 2003, Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during re-entry after a 16-day mission, killing all seven astronauts •⁠ ⁠Commander Rick Husband •⁠ ⁠Pilot William McCool •⁠ ⁠Payload commander Michael Anderson •⁠ ⁠Mission specialists Kalpana Chawla, David Brown and Laurel Clark •⁠ ⁠Payload specialist Ilan Ramon the first Israeli in space

item.title: Dense Fog Triggers 59-Vehicle Pileup On California Highway, Injures 10
item.description: A massive 59-vehicle pileup injured at least 10 people Saturday on California’s Highway 99, authorities said. The California Highway Patrol reported dense fog in Tulare County at the time of the crashes, reducing visibility to just 100–200 feet.

item.title: Icicles Form In Florida As Arctic Blast Brings Extreme Cold
item.description: Icicles formed in Lakeland, Florida as freezing temperatures swept across the state this weekend. An arctic blast tightening its grip on the East Coast has prompted Extreme Cold Warnings for parts of Florida through Monday morning.
